quote: PDF p99, note 26 Technical Provisions (continued): 'The reconciliation of opening and closing provision for claims is as follows:' 2024 Gross | RI | Net $000: At 1 January 3,173,914 | (1,350,678) | 1,823,236; RITC adjustment - | - | -; Adjusted 1 January 3,173,914 | (1,350,678) | 1,823,236; Claims paid during the year (1,149,485) | 488,387 | (661,098); Expected cost of current year claims 1,539,495 | (478,413) | 1,061,082; Change in estimates of prior year provisions (89,063) | 27,677 | (61,386); Foreign exchange (44,966) | 11,554 | (33,412); At 31 December 3,429,895 | (1,301,473) | 2,128,422. PDF p81, note 7, 2024 Total: Gross claims incurred (1,450,432).
arithmetic: Filing gross prior-year line (89,063) $000 = -89.063m. Adopted -89.1m. |diff| = 0.037 <= tolerance max(0.5, 0.05 x 89.1 = 4.455) = 4.455; same sign (release). Checks: gross roll-forward 3,173,914 - 1,149,485 + 1,539,495 - 89,063 - 44,966 = 3,429,895, the printed At 31 December. The prior-year line is incurred development, not a provision-only change: 1,539,495 - 89,063 = 1,450,432, which is note 7's 2024 gross claims incurred (p81).
basis_check: Gross: the line is in the Gross column of note 26's claims reconciliation (RI 27,677; Net (61,386)). The directors' report 'positive prior year reserve development of $61m (2023: $14m)' (p11) is the net column: (61,386) and 2023 (13,782). The adopted -89.1 is the gross figure.
page_binding_check: This syndicate's figure. The filing is a single-syndicate report: every page is headed 'Syndicate 4444 Annual Report & Accounts 31 December 2024', and note 26 is PDF p99 (printed 'Page 49 of 51'). The brief's cited pages do not follow PDF order: PDF p21 is the auditor's report and p5 the contents page. gpt-5-mini's pages 49 and 16 are the printed numbers of note 26 and the liabilities balance sheet.
triangle_arithmetic: Not the scored route: the route is rag_provisions, the pack says the stored triangle was overruled by the sign veto, and there is no CODE OVERRIDE, so the numeric field is left null. For information only: the stored grid matches the printed gross table on PDF p53 ('Gross of reinsurance', $'000, 'At end of underwriting year' ..., 'presented at the exchange rates prevailing at 31 December 2024') cell by cell for UW 2015-2023. Last-diagonal steps, UW 2015-2022: 2015 904,220-904,170 = +50; 2016 1,050,466-1,051,731 = -1,265; 2017 1,327,851-1,331,442 = -3,591; 2018 1,121,303-1,119,964 = +1,339; 2019 1,492,735-1,434,884 = +57,851; 2020 1,115,347-1,150,582 = -35,235; 2021 1,115,866-1,110,775 = +5,091; 2022 1,185,804-1,094,754 = +91,050; sum +115,290 = +115.29m.
reasoning: The filing states the gross prior-year movement explicitly (note 26, Gross column). Under the protocol that is the filing's figure, and the adopted -89.1 agrees within tolerance. It covers prior years only, since current-year claims are a separate row. The underwriting-year triangle on p53 sums to +115.29m. It is a cumulative underwriting-year table at 31 December 2024 exchange rates, not a stated prior-year movement, and the protocol uses a triangle only when no explicit gross movement is given. So it does not make the record undeterminable. The $61m in the directors' report is the net column.

takeon_base.carried: No business came into the syndicate in 2024. The adopted figure is note 26's gross prior-year line. It follows an 'RITC adjustment' row that is nil in the 2024 columns (nil also in notes 25 and 26 for DAC and UPR, and in the level 3 note). The only take-on was the RITC of Syndicate 1861's 2020 year of account into this syndicate's 2021 year of account. It happened on 1 January 2023, an earlier year (2023 RITC adjustment 398,720 gross), so the 1 January 2024 opening of 3,173,914 already holds it. The LPT the scan found was entered into in 2021 and is outward: its premium sat in reinsurance ceded creditors. The Part VII transfer to Lloyd's Brussels, reinsured back on 30 December 2020, is an earlier year. The closure of the 2022 YoA into the 2023 YoA is internal and after the balance sheet date.
takeon_base.evidence: p99 note 26 claims reconciliation (2024 Gross RI Net | 2023 Restated Gross RI Net): 'RITC adjustment 1 - - - 398,720 (187,550) 211,170'. Footnote: '2023 RITC adjustment: On 1 January 2023 the 2021 year of account of the Syndicate accepted the RITC of the 2020 year of account of Syndicate 1861.' p95 note 22: 'Reinsurance ceded 526,043 680,776 ... Reinsurance ceded in 2023 included the balance of premium due in relation to the LPT entered into in 2021.' p81 note 7: 'Underwriting results for those policies transferred to Lloyd's Brussels via Part VII transfer and subsequently reinsured back to the Syndicate on 30 December 2020 have been reported under the inwards reinsurance class of business'. p99 note 28: 'On 18 February 2025 the Board of the Managing Agent authorised the closure of the 2022 year of account by way of reinsurance to close into the 2023 year of account.'

quote: PDF p18 (printed page 15), Notes to the Financial Statements at 31 December 2014: '2. Claims Outstanding Reassessment of claims outstanding on underwriting years 2011 & prior (2013 – 2010 & prior) resulted in an improvement of £41.2 m (2013 – £28.7m).'
arithmetic: An improvement (release) of £41.2m = -41.2m. Adopted -41.2m. |diff| = 0.0 <= tolerance max(0.5, 0.05 x 41.2 = 2.06) = 2.06; same sign. Scope: underwriting years 2011 & prior. That excludes the two most recent underwriting years (2013, 2014), and the figure is a one-year reassessment, not a cohort's cumulative total. It also leaves out UW 2012, which a triangle sum up to t-2 would include. The filing prints no triangle, and this is the prior-year movement it states.
basis_check: Not stated. Note 2 does not say gross or net, and the note is referenced both from the gross 'Claims outstanding' liability (p16: 543,606 / 378,654) and from the reinsurers' share asset (p15: 72,025 / 53,450). Directors' report p4: favourable development on the back years 'contributed £38.4m to the result' and gave 'a saving of 13 % on the loss ratio'. The loss ratio KPI is net: 131,199 / 322,560 = 40.7%, printed 41% (p13). 41.2 / 322.56 = 12.8%, which rounds to 13%. That is consistent with £41.2m but does not fix its basis. Nothing in the filing makes plain that £41.2m is net, so there is no basis-net error.
page_binding_check: This syndicate's figure. It is in Syndicate 609's own 2014 annual accounts (page header 'SYNDICATE 609 ANNUAL ACCOUNTS 2014', notes at 31 December 2014), PDF p18 = printed page 15, and not in the 2012 year of account underwriting accounts bound in the same PDF (PDF pp. 25-49). The brief's cited pages do not follow PDF order: PDF p7 is the directors' report risk and board section and p5 is investment performance. gpt-5-mini's pages 15 and 13 are the printed numbers of note 2 and the liabilities balance sheet. Syndicate 570 has no separate report in this filing: its 2011 year of account was reinsured to close into 609, so in 2014 that business is 609's.
triangle_arithmetic: Not applicable. The route is a model reading of note 2 (source None, no CODE OVERRIDE). The filing prints no claims development triangle: the pack records 'no triangle in report', and a page-tool search of the filing for development/triangle finds only narrative and accounting-policy text.
reasoning: Note 2 states the prior-year movement explicitly, and the adopted -41.2 equals it with the same sign. Its basis is not stated. Because the filing does not make plain that it is net, the protocol's basis error does not apply. The directors' report £38.4m is a contribution to the result, not a reassessment of claims outstanding, so I do not treat it as a competing figure for the gross prior-year development (read as one, its 2.8m gap would exceed the 2.06m tolerance). The route is a model reading and the filing has no triangle.

takeon_base.carried: The adopted figure is note 2's one-line reassessment of claims outstanding on underwriting years 2011 & prior; there is no roll-forward and no triangle. Syndicate 570's 2011 year of account, with the prior years reinsured into it, came into 609's 2012 year of account with effect from 1 January 2014. So through 2014 it was part of 609's claims outstanding on underwriting years 2011 & prior, which is exactly the scope of the reassessment. The directors compare the 2014 back-year saving of 13% (41.2 / 322.56 = 12.8%) with the '2013 Combined Syndicate' (570 + 609) figure, which places the 2014 figure on the merged book. Note 2's own 2013 comparative (£28.7m, 8.8% of 609's 2013 NEP of 324.5) does not match the combined 13%, consistent with 609 alone. The opening reserves exclude the transfer. The 31 December 2013 comparatives are 609 alone: 2013 GWP of 380,441 is the KPI table's '609' column, not 'Combined' 378.5. The transfer was booked straight to the balance sheet in 2014: gross claims outstanding rose from 378,654 to 543,606, but the technical account's gross change in the provision for claims is only 498, and GWP of 365,018 carries no RITC premium. The filing does not state the gross reserves transferred from 570 on their own, so takeon_amount_m is null. The only RITC amounts it states are the 2012 YoA's combined RITC receivable, which includes 609's own 2011 YoA (already in the opening) as well as 570's 2011 YoA: gross notified outstanding claims 141,399 + gross IBNR 180,349 = 321,748 gross, or 279,083 net at transaction rates (p41). The 570 part cannot be split from it.
takeon_base.evidence: p4: 'With effect from 1 January 2014 the 2011 year of account of Syndicate 570 was reinsured to close into the 2012 year of account of Syndicate 609.' and 'As a result, the balance sheet presented in these accounts at 31 December 2014 reflects the effect of the reinsurance to close transaction.' p4: 'the first calendar year result as a merged Syndicate'. p4: 'contributing a saving of 13 % on the loss ratio (2013 Combined Syndicate – 13 %)'. p4 KPIs (2014 609 | 2013 570 | 2013 609 | 2013 Combined, £m): 'Gross premiums written 365.0 (1.9) 380.4 378.5'; 'Net earned premiums 322.6 4.1 324.5 328.6'. p18 note 2: 'Reassessment of claims outstanding on underwriting years 2011 & prior (2013 – 2010 & prior) resulted in an improvement of £41.2 m'. p16 balance sheet: 'Claims outstanding 2 543,606 378,654'. p13 technical account: 'Change in the provision for claims: Gross amount 498 (4,289)'. p41 (2012 YoA accounts) note 2, Reinsurance to Close Premium Receivable: 'Gross notified outstanding claims 141,399'; 'Provision for gross claims incurred but not reported 180,349'; 'Reinsurance to close premium receivable, net of reinsurance at transaction rates of exchange 279,083'.
